How this was solved: counterfactual regret minimization (CFR+) over all 169 starting hands for six players with 100bb stacks and blinds of 0.5 and 1, no antes. Any seat may open (2.2bb or 3bb; the small blind opens to 3bb), call, 3-bet or squeeze. Up to three players can see a flop in a single-raised pot. To keep the game solvable, there are no limps, players who have not entered fold to a 3-bet, and once someone answers a 3-bet or 4-bet the pot is heads-up. The charts list every open and the spots that come up most often. All-ins are valued with exact equity. Pots that reach the flop are valued with estimated equity realization: the player in position realizes more of their equity, and suited, connected and paired hands realize more than offsuit hands. Three-way pots use pairwise equities combined into a three-way share. Treat it as a strong baseline rather than a full postflop solve.
